chapter: Chapter 10. Anatomy of the Great Financial Crisis
stem: A risk consultant is giving a presentation to a group of analysts on subprime mortgages and how they contributed to the 2007–2009 financial crisis. The consultant begins with an overview of the mechanics of subprime mortgages and some subprime market trends in the years leading up to the crisis. Which of the following statements would be correct for the risk consultant to include in the presentation?
stem_short: Which statement about subprime mortgages is correct?

options.A: While housing prices were rising, subprime borrowers typically refinanced adjustable-rate mortgages into a similar mortgage once the teaser rate period ended.
options.B: By securitizing subprime mortgages, banks created asset pools mostly rated below investment grade to sell to investors.
options.C: Demand for subprime financing before the crisis was fueled partly by high interest rates and a strong housing market.
options.D: Under the originate-to-distribute (OTD) model, the bank that originated the loans incurred all the losses.

high.label: THE PATTERN
high.text: Teaser rate ends → refinance into a new similar loan

B.reason: Tranching made most of the pool investment grade, often AAA.

C.reason: Demand was fueled by low rates in the early 2000s.

D.reason: Under OTD, investors who bought the loans bore the losses.

takeaway.text: Teaser rates relied on rising prices

sections.text: [warmly] Hey, welcome back to Risk Hub! FRM Part 1, Book 1, Foundations of Risk Management. Chapter 10, Anatomy of the Great Financial Crisis. Let's do a practice question.

So, a risk consultant is presenting to analysts on subprime mortgages and how they contributed to the 2007 to 2009 financial crisis. The consultant starts with how subprime mortgages worked, and the market trends before the crisis. Which statement is correct to include?

Option A. While house prices were rising, subprime borrowers would typically refinance their adjustable-rate mortgage into a similar one as soon as the teaser rate ended. Option B. By securitizing subprime mortgages, banks created asset pools that were mostly rated below investment grade. Option C. Demand for subprime financing was fueled partly by high interest rates and a strong housing market. And option D. Under the originate-to-distribute model, the bank that made the loans took all the losses.
Okay, pause the video and lock in your answer. [long pause]

[excited] And the answer is... A! [warmly] Here's why. Many subprime loans were adjustable-rate mortgages with a low teaser rate for the first few years. When the teaser period ended, borrowers would simply refinance into another similar mortgage. As long as house prices kept rising, that worked. Once prices stopped rising, it fell apart.

Now, why not the others? B is wrong. Banks sliced the pools into tranches, so most of the value was rated investment grade, often triple A. Only a small equity tranche was below investment grade. C is wrong too. The boom was fueled by low interest rates in the early 2000s, not high ones. And D? Under originate-to-distribute, the banks sold the loans on. The investors who bought them took the losses.

[warmly] So, the key takeaway. Teaser-rate mortgages only worked while house prices kept rising. Low interest rates fueled the housing boom. And originate-to-distribute pushed the losses onto investors. If this helped, follow Risk Hub for more FRM practice. See you in the next one!
